_paths_comment: Portable paths: ${HOUFIN_DATA}/${HOUFIN_PROCESSED} expand at load (src/config_utils.py; default <repo>/data and <repo>/data/processed locally, override via env on HPC). NOTE: the DESK/encoder pipeline is a later milestone; this layout is provisional and its stream wiring (2-stream state_*_bio_ema10 -> N-stream state_*) is still to be reconciled.

states._climate_comment: climate = scheme monthly_bioyear_v2 (climate_grid_monthly): 12 channels per base variable, one per month POSITION in the bio-year window (b01 = bio_year_start_month), values verbatim -- NOT an annual mean. The old climate_grid/ dir held one annual mean/total per base, erasing every within-year contrast (winter severity, seasonality amplitude), so it could not express a seasonality-driven range limit. Elevation levels are asymmetric: q50 for every base, q10/q90 only for Tmin/Tmax/Tave (lapse rate). Authoritative channel ORDER lives in climate_grid_monthly/manifest.json and is validated by build_states.discover_variables -- channel identity is positional and feeds the saved mu/sd, so a silent reorder would misnormalize every channel.
states._bui_comment: bui is ADDITIVE to hyde, not a replacement: HISDAC-US built-up intensity is a much better urbanisation signal (250 m indoor building area, semi-decadal back to 1810) but is CONTERMINOUS-US ONLY, while the grid spans CONUS + southern Canada + a northern-Mexico strip. So the encoder gets BUI where it exists, HYDE everywhere, and bui_avail -- the fraction of each cell with real BUI data -- as an explicit channel of the same stream telling it which regime a cell is in. Folded in rather than given its own stream because a standalone 1-wide stream costs ~500k parameters (+23%): the stream count enters both the mixer and the decoder. indicator_variable does two things: it makes augment.ChannelGroupMasker mask bui_avail atomically with the values, so training never sees 'available' alongside a meanless value, and it makes covariate_io exempt bui_avail from BOTH the transform and the standardization. That exemption is load-bearing. bui_avail is a flag, not a measurement, and it has to reach the encoder as the raw coverage fraction so that 0 means ABSENT -- because the augmentation masks by multiplying by 0. Standardizing it would put absent near -1.2 and make 0 mean 'about 60% covered', a state no real cell is in. transform log1p is mandatory for the quantile bands, not optional: raw BUI is indoor square feet running to ~1e7-1e8 with a heavy right tail. Cells outside the CONUS footprint are filled with a constant per-channel value chosen to land at 0 after standardisation; see src/data/preprocess/bui.py for why that, why not 0, and why not NaN.
states._ema_comment: ema_tau is a LIGHT backward-EMA time constant (~2 yr, half-life ~1.4 yr) applied at state-build time -- just denoises annual weather so the per-year covariate grid is a near-instantaneous suitability signal. It runs per channel ALONG THE YEAR AXIS (a monthly channel like Tmax_b01m08 at year T is an EMA over previous Augusts), never across months, so it does not blur the seasonal structure the monthly channels exist to preserve. The DECADAL demographic lag is NOT here; it lives on the DESK OUTPUT (learned output-EMA, desk.output_ema). Was 10 (~7-yr half-life); reduced so z_raw fluxes and the two lags stay identifiable.

esk._spacetime_comment: Joint spatiotemporal ESK (run_spacetime_esk): uncentered Ružicka Nyström features over the trend-based annual community points. Uncentered is intentional: with an isotropic Bayesian coefficient prior downstream, Z(x)·Z(x') approximates the original Ružicka GP kernel rather than a reference-distribution-centered kernel. 64 dimensions address the measured rank-truncation error; 16k uniform-random landmarks already make landmark error small. sigma=0 because trend points have n_weeks=1. 'diverse' and 'stratified' remain available ablations, not production defaults. Writes esk/spacetime/{Z.npy, valid_mask, esk_landmarks, esk_projmat, meta.json}.
esk._n_landmarks_comment: esk.spacetime.n_landmarks (16000) is the PRODUCTION landmark budget, supported by the measured error decomposition: at 16k the landmark/eigenpair term is small next to the rank-truncation floor. The separate esk.n_landmarks (25000) belongs to the opt-in eBird-only sweep. It used to live under bbs.n_landmarks, which made the production value hard to find and put it two blocks away from the comment explaining it.

_augment_comment: Structured channel-group masking of the DESK covariate input (see src/community_encoder/train_DESK/augment.py). Masks whole GROUPS, not independent channels: the ~295 channels are 14 climate bases x 12 bio-year months x 1-3 elevation quantiles, so a channel's neighbours (adjacent month, other quantile) are near-duplicates and i.i.d. dropout is trivially inpainted. Masking to 0 is exact mean-imputation because covariates are standardized and invalid cells are already zero-filled post-standardization. Survivors are NOT rescaled (this is denoising/MAE augmentation, not unit dropout) and the reconstruction target stays the CLEAN grid, which makes DESK a denoising autoencoder. A fresh mask is drawn per year-forward, so one optimizer step averages ~86 independent draws. p_base drops one base variable across all its months AND levels; p_month drops one bio-year month position across all bases; span_prob/span_max drop a CONTIGUOUS run of months (harder to inpaint than i.i.d. ones, and the bio-year is a window so there is no wraparound); p_level drops the temperature-only q10/q90; p_stream drops a whole stream but NEVER climate (240/295 channels -- that would blind the model). max_masked_frac redraws any degenerate sample. Set enabled=false to recover the un-augmented recipe.

augment._tile_comment: tile_cells sets the SPATIAL granularity of the masking. 0 = one draw shared by the whole grid, which gives temporal diversity but none spatially: every cell sees the same variables missing, so nothing teaches the encoder that different regions must cope with losing different ones. Since the holdout is spatially BLOCKED, spatial generalization is exactly what is measured -- and the observed gap is a 4.8x train/val MSE ratio with rotation at ~1.00 on train and ~0.86 on val. Kept at or below trend.block_cells so the masking varies at a scale no coarser than the evaluation unit: at 6 a tile IS a holdout block. Costs ~0.83 s/epoch (874 draws/mask) vs 0.37 s at 12 and 0 when disabled -- ~7 min over 500 epochs, measured. 0 restores the old grid-wide behaviour.
augment._persist_comment: PERSISTENCE tier -- a second draw taken ONCE per optimizer step and held across all years of the window, multiplied into the per-year draw, so a group goes missing for the WHOLE window rather than one year. MEASURED AND TURNED OFF; do not re-enable without new evidence. Ablation at 500 epochs, single change, everything else fixed: WITH persist Val 0.0827 / rot va 0.58 / raw va 1.05 / train 0.0575; WITHOUT Val 0.0796 / rot va 0.64 / raw va 1.12 / train 0.0544. Both splits improved without it, so the train/val ratio was unchanged at ~1.45x -- it cost temporal amplitude and bought no generalization. The rationale does not survive scrutiny either: it was meant to teach the encoder to cope with a structurally absent covariate (BUI is CONUS-only), but BUI absence is ALREADY a real observed regime in every training year over ~63% of cells, flagged by bui_avail. Augmentation is for missingness the model would NOT otherwise see; the same point applies to LUH-3 post-2024 and HYDE pre-1951. The machinery stays -- tested, zero cost when off, and legitimate for a covariate complete in training but absent at inference, which none here are. To re-enable, add a persist block with nonzero rates; augment.persist defaults to all-zero.

_target_comment: WHICH point set supervises the encoder. bbs_raw is what the surveyors counted: raw route-level BBS community counts aggregated to the 27 km grid (1.08 routes per cell-year, so that aggregation is very nearly a no-op), plus the eBird trend product INSIDE its own window as a second target, the two put on one scale by an explicit calibration. The retired alternative, trend_products, reconstructed each cell from ~4 time-invariant numbers and then smoothed it spatially, which made an interpolator near-optimal on it by construction -- val MSE never beat inverse-distance-8 in any run (1.49x, 1.97x, 2.10x, 2.02x worse). Point target.points_dir at the trend_products output to run that A/B. Measured on the raw target: median off-diagonal Ruzicka 0.197, with same-cell-different-year pairs at 0.649 against different-cell pairs at 0.197 -- a 3.3x separation, versus a reconstructed target sitting near the 'similarity ~1.0 means underpowered' failure mode.

target._bbs_comment: first_year_weight downweights cell-years surveyed by an observer in their first year on that route -- the one part of the bbsBayes2 observer submodel that ports to a non-Bayesian target (there it is eta*first_year[i], one coefficient on a 0/1 column, grouped by observer x ROUTE so an experienced observer moving route is flagged again). Weighted rather than dropped because those cell-years still carry real absences. The cost is era-correlated: the first-year share is 25.6% in 1966-1980 against 12.3% in 2001-2025, so this thins the early era -- the invasion front -- about twice as hard as the modern one. 0.5 retains ~92% of effective supervision overall, 0.75 retains ~96%. temporal_ema_tau smooths within a cell across years and is OFF (0) by default: temporal smoothing at a fixed location borrows no power across space, so it is defensible in a way spatial smoothing is not, but it has to earn its place by measurement.
target._ebird_window_comment: OFF. The encoder trains on raw BBS alone. Fitted on the real products, the two surveys correlate a median 0.405 per species across 379,246 paired cell-years, and ~80% of eBird's spread is unexplained by BBS -- against the ~1% a product an order of magnitude more trustworthy would show. Much of that surplus is real rather than error: eBird resolves spatial structure BBS cannot see at 27 km, and the two have different sampling emphases. But it means they are not close measurements of one quantity, and putting both in one similarity kernel would ask the encoder to reproduce both. Setting enabled=true restores the multi-task target: eBird supervises only inside its own 2012-2022 window, calibrated onto the BBS scale by train_DESK/bbs_ebird_calibration.py, and lifts supervised cells from ~3,900 to ~17,200 for that window.
target._calibration_comment: Only used when ebird_window.enabled is true. Puts BBS counts and eBird abundances on a common scale via a latent-abundance model: one true abundance per cell-year, seen by BBS as a Poisson count and by eBird as a continuous modelled index. BBS's measurement noise is DERIVED rather than fitted -- a Poisson count with mean B has log-variance about 1/B, so rare species are automatically noisier -- which identifies the model with no search, cap, or free noise parameter. eBird's noise then falls out and is compared against trust_ratio as a CHECK; assuming it too would over-determine the model. Species exponents and scales are partially pooled with continuous shrinkage and no cutoffs. See the module docstring for the full model.

_trend_reference_comment: The trend products rebuilt as a SANITY-CHECK REFERENCE rather than a training target, read by train_DESK/validate_trend_reference.py. Two differences from the trend block: smooth_sigma_cells is 0, and it writes to its own points_dir so the reference and the training target coexist. The blur existed to stabilise a training target and there is no target to stabilise any more -- leaving it on would mean the panel's pure-spatial comparison grades the model against OUR smoothing of the products rather than against the products, making a poor score there unattributable. The soft caps deliberately stay on (inherited from the trend block): their stabilising purpose is gone but their outlier-control purpose is not, and a handful of 100x-fold extrapolations would dominate exactly the RMSE and rank statistics the panel's comparisons 2 and 4 use.
_trend_comment: Trend-product spatiotemporal community target (trend_community.build_trend_points). Applies published %/yr trends to the 2023 eBird annual anchor, blending eBird recent (2012-2022) and BBS long-term (1966-2022) rates with a smooth handoff, integrated backward to first_year. Paths (bbs_trend_grid, ebird_trend_grid, community_trend_list) fall back to data_config; ebird_weekly_grid falls back to paths.ebird_folder.

trend._anchor_comment: anchor_mode=trends-abd (default): the reference-year abundance E is the eBird trends product's own midpoint reference `abd` (rel-abundance at (start_year+end_year)/2, ~2017), forward-extrapolated to anchor_year along abd_ppy: E = abd*(1+abd_ppy/100)^(anchor_year-mid). Same product+cells as the rate (no coverage mismatch); needs NO weekly eBird download. anchor_mode=weekly is the legacy path (2023 annual mean of the weekly status rasters; needs the projected weekly grid + --require-weekly download). anchor_year=2025 is the reference year (end of the covariate timeline); reconstruction compounds backward from it. Both abd_ppy (eBird) and tr{AOU} (BBS) are percent-PER-YEAR.
trend._stride_comment: point_year_stride=1: emit EVERY year 1966-2025, so the ESK basis input and the DESK per-year targets are fully spatiotemporal (not just endpoints). ESK landmark subsampling keeps the Nystrom eigh bounded.
trend._points_dir_comment: Where build_trend_points writes the ESK INPUT point set (X_points.npy, point_index.npy, points_meta.json). Distinct from desk.z_dir, which is the ESK OUTPUT basis (esk/spacetime). Those two used to be bbs.z_dir and desk.z_dir -- one character apart, holding opposite things.
trend._cap_comment: TWO overlapping globally smooth p-softsign caps on the backward change: C_p(x; A)=x/(1+(|x|/A)^p)^(1/p). Both use p=2: unit slope at zero and smooth saturation, with no knee/elbow. (1) RELATIVE/fold cap on log(N/E), asymptoting at soft_max_fold=100; protects rare-base cells. (2) ABSOLUTE cap on (N-E), asymptoting at abs_soft_max_mult times each species' p95 occupied-cell present abundance; limits a worst-cell -> good-habitat jump. Neither is community-relative. smooth_sigma_cells>0 adds a post-cap masked Gaussian on log-abundance (in cells) so a capped extreme cannot poison neighbours (0 = off).
trend._coverage_comment: Per-cell, per-year coverage gate: emit a historical (cell,year) community point only if >= min_coverage of the cell's occupying species have a trend informing that year (eBird when the blend leans recent, BBS when deep). Prevents false-stability points where most species would be held constant (~23% of cells have <50% deep BBS coverage). The recent anchor year is always kept.

bbs._comment: BBS community settings. LIVE on the pipeline: community_axes and species_list (community selection, read by identify/*), turnover_min_gap (the validate stage) and ebird_stack_cache (the opt-in ebird-cache stage). The community_matrix path and the smoothing/anomaly knobs below are read ONLY by the raw-BBS turnover diagnostic, scripts/viz/raw_bbs_turnover.py -- they are not pipeline inputs. The ESK point set moved to trend.points_dir and the production landmark budget to esk.spacetime.n_landmarks; both used to live here, which is why the production values were hard to find.
bbs._community_axes_comment: The reference community is the UNION of four per-axis top-N cuts (phylo-nearest, morphology-nearest, urban-loving, urban-avoiding), taken AFTER the BBS/eBird trend-product gates -- see identify/community_axes.py. n_per_axis=30 lands the union near 100, matching the previous community size. max_migratory_frac is the knob you actually set: the selector solves for the SMALLEST migration rank penalty achieving it, because pool-rank units are arbitrary (a fixed penalty drifts in meaning if the gate or the pool changes) while a stated composition does not. Migrants are downweighted because Z encodes local year-round suitability from year-round covariates, and a long-distance migrant's June abundance is driven by wintering-ground and flyway dynamics the model has no covariates for. The penalty is additive on the pool rank and zero for sedentary species, so raising it can never displace a non-migrant; the interpretable form is the per-class admission bar the selector logs. penalty_max only bounds the search. 0.30 rather than a tighter ceiling because the candidate pool is 53% migratory, and squeezing to 0.20 needs p=30 -- which drives the urban_loving axis's migratory admission bar NEGATIVE (-13), i.e. no migrant can place on it at all, however urban-tolerant. At 0.30 the solver lands on p=19 and all four bars stay positive (urban_loving 6), so every axis still downweights migrants without any axis excluding them outright.
bbs._community_top_n_comment: NOT the community size -- community_axes sets that. This is only the default --top-n for the standalone identify/bbs_crosswalk.py diagnostic CLI, which reports how far down the candidate pool the AOU join succeeds.
bbs._smooth_comment: Gaussian NW smoothing in GRID CELLS (25 km). sigma_s=2 (~50 km stdev, ~100 km 2-sigma reach) connects nearby BBS routes without continental blur; the raw-BBS diagnostic showed sigma_s=5 kept only ~65% of real per-cell change vs ~78% at sigma_s=2. Coverage is now handled by the relative support floor, so sigma_s no longer needs to be large. No expansion-front concern: House Finch (the transfer target) is excluded from the community.
bbs._ablation_comment: Suppression knobs still at the max-permissive ablation values (pseudocount 0.1, shrink_k 0, cap ln100, sigma_t 1) so this run isolates the bbs_community species fix + sigma_s reduction against the prior ablation run. Restore moderate robustness (shrink_k~1, cap ln10, pseudocount 0.5) for a production config once attribution is settled.

desk._label_year_comment: label_year = the anchor/reference year (matches trend.anchor_year). The Ružicka metric is anchored on the reconstructed year-label_year community, and the output-EMA window runs [output_ema.warmup_start .. label_year].
desk._train_comment: epochs is an UPPER BOUND; early stopping on held-out Stab(val) (patience) restores the best weights, so a long budget is safe. 100 epochs left every loss still descending (undertrained) -> raised to 500. GPU memory is dominated by the RESIDENT year window: the trainer forwards the whole warmup_start..label_year window every step so the causal output-EMA can run over the year axis, which at ~295 channels is ~3 GB before gradients. A CUDA OOM here means shortening that window (output_ema.warmup_start) or narrowing hidden_width -- there is no per-step batching knob to lower. (There was: batch_years, which only ever controlled the reconstruction grids in the retired non-EMA trainer.)
desk._patience_comment: Set to epochs so early stopping cannot fire: the warmup+cosine schedule anneals over `epochs`, and stopping at ~247 previously left the LR at 57% of peak with the BEST weights taken at 72% -- the model never settled. Best-checkpoint restore still applies, so a late best epoch is itself the evidence that annealing matters. Lower this again only alongside an `epochs` that the run actually reaches.
desk._optim_comment: AdamW: weight_decay applies to matmul weights only (LayerNorm gains, biases, and the scalars gamma/theta are excluded -- decaying a gate or a learned half-life is an unasked-for prior). LR is warmup+cosine, NOT ReduceLROnPlateau: the EMA trainer takes ONE step per epoch (the sequential year scan forces a full-window step), so the whole run is <=epochs updates and a plateau patience of 5 against an early-stop patience of 50 just chased noise. dropout is the rate inside every BMLPBlock; it was hardcoded at 0.5, which is very aggressive for a regression autoencoder and now compounds with input masking (see the top-level augment block) -- hence 0.1. amp = bf16 autocast on the per-year forward only (no GradScaler needed); the EMA scan and all losses stay fp32 because 86 sequential bf16 accumulations drift. eval_every>1 amortizes the clean eval re-forward.
desk._capacity_comment: hidden_width is the per-branch width h (null = the historical max(128, latent_dim*4) = 256). Branch params scale as h^2, so 128 cuts them from 5.34M to ~1.33M and the whole net from 7.63M to ~3.6M. Generalization here is measured along the SPATIAL axis (the holdout is blocked by cell) and there are only ~12,263 training cells, i.e. ~620 params/cell at h=256 -- the measured symptom is a 4.8x train/val MSE gap with rotation ~1.00 on train vs ~0.86 on val. hidden_width and mlp_expansion set state_dict SHAPES and are persisted to desk_meta.npz; the cube and validate read them back, so old checkpoints keep loading.
desk._weights_comment: stabilizing is per-ELEMENT now (the term is divided by latent_dim), so this weight absorbs the old latent_dim factor: 64.0 here == the previous 1.0 on a 64-dim SUM, numerically identical at latent_dim=64 but with all three weights finally on the same scale. The per-epoch log prints each term's weighted share of the total, so the real mix is observable.
desk._spatial_conv_comment: Tight residual masked (partial) conv on the latent grid: injects neighbourhood context a point-wise encoder cannot learn. gamma inits 0 so training starts as the exact point-wise, ESK-aligned model. kernel=5 => 5x5 (two 27 km rings, +/-54 km). NOTE the validation buffer width is DERIVED from this as kernel//2 (see trend.block_cells) -- widening the kernel automatically widens the buffer, because a prediction at a val cell reads cells up to kernel//2 away.
desk._trend_comment: The training objective. DESK predicts per-year z_raw from (lightly-smoothed) covariates, applies a LEARNED causal output-EMA over the year axis (output_ema) to get z_ema, and supervises z_ema against the trend-based spatiotemporal z-target -- every (cell,year) point EQUAL weight. The output-EMA models demographic lag: the year-Y community is a leaky integral of past suitability, so per-year predictions flux with the environment while the supervised decadal estimate is a stable mixture of recent years. holdout_frac of eBird cells withheld for honest z-space eval.
desk._trend_split_comment: Validation is SPATIALLY BLOCKED, not an i.i.d. cell draw: with a k x k latent conv and strongly autocorrelated covariates, scattered held-out cells are surrounded by training cells and the metric flatters itself. Whole block_cells x block_cells tiles go to validation, and a buffer ring of kernel//2 cells is dilated OUTWARD from each block and excluded from both training and the normalization fit -- so val blocks stay intact at any block size and the minimum val-to-train separation is always kernel//2. block_cells sets the MAXIMUM extrapolation depth: (block/2 + buffer) cells from the nearest training data. Measured on the real 17,209-cell footprint: block 12 / frac 0.2 gave 12,180 training cells, 216 km max depth, 45 val blocks; block 6 / frac 0.1 gives 13,220 training cells, 135 km max depth, 87 val blocks -- better on all three, because buffer overhead grows as blocks shrink (perimeter/area) and is paid back by the smaller holdout fraction. Reduced to 6/0.1 after the 12/0.2 split showed DESK losing to the no-change null on held-out cells (err ratio 1.21x, beats in 34%), i.e. 216 km extrapolation was beyond what the covariates support. holdout_years withholds a contiguous span of supervised years for a TEMPORAL val metric (Val(yr-out)); label_year is never withheld since it carries the eBird metric loss. Diagnostic only: model selection stays on the spatial metric.
desk._holdout_frac_comment: Raised 0.1 -> 0.15 because the split is now drawn over cells that CARRY SUPERVISION rather than over the eBird covariate footprint. Those were nearly the same (~17,200 cells) while the target was an interpolated surface covering everything; a measured target is not -- raw BBS reaches ~3,900 cells and BBS+eBird ~12,400 -- so the same fraction of a smaller domain yields far fewer validation cells. min_val_cells is a hard floor: below it, best-epoch selection itself rests on too few cells to mean anything, so the run stops rather than reporting a number nobody should trust.
desk._output_ema_comment: Learned causal EMA over the year axis on PREDICTED z during supervision. half_life is learned in half_life_bounds and saved to desk_meta for provenance/diagnostics. build_final_z_cube intentionally exports z_raw without reapplying this EMA because the population model supplies lagged demographic response.
desk._zdir_comment: The JOINT uncentered spatiotemporal ESK basis (esk/spacetime). latent_dim=64 is the production GP feature width; it must match esk.spacetime.latent_dim and the age model's source_latent_dim. The age model's own latent_dim (24) is a further truncation of that, not the same number.

latent_cube._radius_comment: Gap-fill footprint in KM; build_final_z_cube converts to pixels at the model grid (radius_km/res_km), so it is resolution-independent. 100 km -> ~4 px at 27 km.
